name: the creation
lore:
Before the First Age, the world was a crucible of unrefined wonder. In this era of Creation, ecology was not a cycle of decay, but a violent surge of vitality. The land breathed; the first forests did not merely bloom—they conquered, their roots drinking directly from the raw, unfiltered Weave.

Behavior in this dawn was defined by a singular, primal majesty. The Firstborn—beasts of mountain-scale and elemental temperament—moved with tectonic intent, carving valleys with their passage. They lacked the skittishness of modern prey, for they knew no predators save the gods themselves. These titans existed in a state of perpetual, rhythmic expansion, driven by the planet’s own quickening pulse. To witness them was to see life in its most honest form: a relentless, beautiful hunger to exist, unburdened by the shadows of mortality or the taming hand of civilization.
